findings.message: The first granule position is 48000 samples beyond what the packets before it hold, so the stream starts at a later time, as a stream cut from a longer one does (RFC 7845, section 4.5).

The first granule position is 960 samples smaller than what the packets before it hold, which gives a negative start; RFC 7845 allows that only on the end-of-stream page, and decoders treat the stream as invalid (section 4.5).

1 granule position before the last page is smaller than the samples of the packets before it: the first, at 0x7B0, is 9550 where the packets give 9600. RFC 7845 allows trimming the end only on the end-of-stream page (section 4.4).
The last granule position, 17200 at 0xBBD, trims 2000 samples from the end, more than the 960 of the last packet, which RFC 7845 asks trimming not to exceed (section 4.4).
The pre-skip of 30000 samples and the end trimming of 0 remove more than the 19200 samples the packets hold, so the stream plays nothing.
The last granule position, 19700 at 0x122B, is 500 samples beyond what the packets before it hold; decoders end the stream earlier than it says.
The page that ends the identification header has the granule position 5, where pages of headers have 0 (RFC 7845, section 3).
The identification header does not end its page, where RFC 7845 starts the next packet on a fresh page (section 3).
The comment header does not end its page, where RFC 7845 starts the next packet on a fresh page (section 3).
